note: The only unanchored question in the set, and therefore the only one where precision is not free. Gold is the account set of every 3-cycle whose hops all ride high-risk channels and which closes inside 24 hours: 9 rings out of 694,703 in the graph, so returning a superset costs real precision. Counts are a lower bound over nodes with out-degree <= 40, because the unbounded two-path join exhausts 10 GB on this graph.
vacuous_predicate_note: Requiring every amount below the CTR threshold was tested and left the count unchanged (13,619 -> 13,619): this generator's base amounts are always sub-threshold. Shipping it as a filter would claim a discrimination it does not perform.

cases.question: Compliance has asked for a proactive sweep — no specific account is under review. Which accounts are part of a three-account transfer cycle where every hop used a high-risk channel and the whole cycle closed within 24 hours? List the account numbers.
cases.scenario: unanchored ring detection against incidental cycles
cases.typology: Layering — rapid circular flow over low-traceability rails
cases.source: FATF layering typology (funds returning to origin have no economic purpose) combined with FATF Professional Money Laundering (2018) on MVTS/hawala and virtual-asset rails; FFIEC BSA/AML red flags on rapid movement
cases.why_it_matters: Every other question in this set names the account to investigate, which hands the agent its anchor and makes precision automatic. A proactive sweep does not: the answer has to be separated from 694,703 structurally identical cycles. This is the question a graph is supposed to be good at, and the first one here that can actually be scored on precision rather than recall.
